title: Trading with a plan
summary: Trade when it helps your plan: when you are cramped, when you are ahead, or when the ending is won. Look at the retake first.
body:
### Trade with a reason

A trade is a plan, not a habit. Before you trade, ask: who gains from it?

These trades often help:

- **You have less space.** A cramped side needs room. Each trade gives your pieces more room.
- **You are ahead in material.** Your extra material counts more when fewer pieces stay on the board. Trade pieces, not pawns.
- **The trade removes the key piece of your opponent.** It can be his best piece, a defender or an attacker.
- **The ending is won.** Count the pawn ending before you trade into it.

These trades often hurt:

- You attack, and the trade removes one of your attackers.
- You have more space, and the trade gives your opponent room.
- You are behind in material, and the trade makes the gap more serious.

Look at the retake. Ask what the position looks like after your opponent takes back. A trade can change the pawn shape and open a file for him.

A pawn ending is easy to count, so use it. If you can win the pawn ending, trade rooks into it. If the pawn ending is only a draw, think again before you trade.

Rule of thumb: trade when it helps your plan, and look at the position after the retake.

exercises.prompt: Black to move. White has more space. Attack the bishop on g5 with your f6 knight.
exercises.explanation: Ne4 attacks the bishop on g5 and the knight on c3. It offers a trade, and a cramped side wants trades. In the engine line White plays Bf4 Nd6, and Black has more room. White still has the better game, about 53 % against 47 %. The other plan moves, such as ...Ng6 and ...a5, are within one win % of ...Ne4.

exercises.prompt: White to move. You are a knight up. Trade your bishop on g5 for the bishop on e7.
exercises.explanation: This is the Carlsbad position, but Black has no knight on f8. White is a knight up, so each trade helps. Bxe7 Qxe7 trades a pair and keeps the extra knight. The engine line is Bxe7 Qxe7 Ra1 Bf5. Bf4 and h4 also keep a big edge, but they keep more black pieces on the board. Nxe4 dxe4 Bxe4 Bxg5 gives Black counterplay; the engine rates it about 87 %, against about 94 % for Bxe7.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Trade rooks: take the rook on d8.
exercises.explanation: Rxd8 Kxd8 hxg5 wins the pawn on g5, and the pawn ending is won. The engine line is Rxd8 Kxd8 hxg5 Kc7 b4 Kd6 Ke4 h4. Rd3 also offers a trade. After Rxd3+ Kxd3 g4, White has no extra pawn, and the engine rates it about 53 %. The trade on d8 wins a pawn, and the engine rates it about 91 %.
